title: feat: implementation of `contrast-color()` from the CSS Color 5
author: yisibl
summary: Parses `contrast-color(<color>)` into a new CssColor::ContrastColor / UnresolvedColor::ContrastColor variant and minifies the inner color. The maintainer asked for the function to be computed to black/white at build time when the color is known (scoping #808 down to level 5), which changes the AST shape, and the author wanted to defer that. Also, nested calls are flattened incorrectly.
evidence: devongovett 2026-03-09: "I think `contrast-color` with a known value should compute to either `black` or `white` at build time, similar to how we calculate the value of relative colors and `color-mix`" and "It would change what gets stored in the AST though right? We wouldn't need a `CssColor::ContrastColor` variant if we parsed it directly to a color." No reply since. Bug in PR: tests expect `contrast-color(contrast-color(blue))` -> `contrast-color(#00f)`, but contrast-color(blue)=white and contrast-color(white)=black, so flattening flips the result. Master already passes it through and minifies the inner color as tokens: `contrast-color(rgb(70 130 180))` -> `contrast-color(#4682b4)`. Older competing PR #808 is open too.
draft:
Thanks for picking this up! Following up on the earlier discussion: since `contrast-color()` with a known color always resolves to `white` or `black`, could this compute it at build time, like we do for `color-mix()` and relative colors? Then the AST wouldn't need a separate `ContrastColor` variant, and only the `var()`/`currentColor` cases would stay unresolved.

One correctness issue in the current version: nested calls are flattened, so `contrast-color(contrast-color(blue))` becomes `contrast-color(blue)`. In browsers the inner call gives `white` and the outer one gives `black`, while the flattened version gives `white`, so it flips the color. Computing the value would fix this for known colors; for unresolved ones the nesting needs to stay as written.
